_help: User rules: original sentence in 'text' + structured 'rules'. target: { items: [ids] } | { groups: [names] } | { tags: [...] } | { all: true, except: { groups: [...] } }. rule types: onFloor, upright, noRotate, noLoadOnTop, maxLoadOnTop {kg}, maxHeight {cm | belowRoofCm}, minHeight {cm}, zone {end: cab|door, withinCm}, loadGroup {n} (1 = loaded first, cab end), exclude, flex, optional (packed after all must-have items, dropped first). 'hard': false makes a zone a preference instead of a must.

constraints.text: Boxes go last: fit the non-box items first, then fill the rest with boxes and bags. Boxes are the first thing we take out if there isn't enough space.
We should start with the large items on the side.
constraints.note: on again 2026-10-29: user wants the large pieces in first because it makes sense to pack small things on top; no fixed order among them (not vitrine-then-bed); 'on the side' (along the walls) is not a rule type, only the loading order

constraints.text: Keyboard is fragile and should be on the top and somewhat sheltered.
constraints.note: lies flat and nothing goes on it (item flags upright + noTop); loaded right after the large pieces, lands on top of them (bottom edge at least 90 cm up) in the cab half, away from the door, with the later small things around it

constraints.text: We will unpack some stuff at the border where we will be weighed, so put some heavy stuff at the back to get heavy stuff out more easily. Not just boxes: the table is super heavy, the plants are heavy, take heavy stuff out.
constraints.note: border stash, loaded last within 180 cm of the door: cartons 200 kg, plants 40, suitcases 62, fireplace 20, desk tops 24 (+ table top, c10); the Iveco is 104 kg over its payload (171 kg with Michelle); by kg per litre the desk tops, table top and suitcases beat the cartons, the plants are heavy per lift but bulky

constraints.text: The table is super heavy. We could do that last.
constraints.note: table top (30 kg) is the very last thing in, so it is the first thing out at the border
